identity.title: The SlHYL1-SlRBP1 module integrates gibberellin metabolism to promote plant height in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum).

content.abstract: Plant height is an essential agronomic trait that significantly influences crop yield and quality. The HYPONASTIC LEAVES 1 (HYL1), a core component of microRNA biogenesis, remains poorly understood in terms of its regulatory mechanisms on agronomic traits in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum, Sl). In this study, we demonstrated that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of SlHYL1 caused dwarfism, and partial suppression of SlHYL1 in tomato cultivar "Ailsa Craig" (AC) via RNA interference (RNAi) increased internode number but reduced internode length, resulting in a semi-dwarf phenotype, confirming the role of SlHYL1 in regulating plant height. Cytological analysis showed that SlHYL1 suppression decreased both cell number and size within internodes. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified that SlHYL1 interacted with another tomato RNA-binding protein 1 (SlRBP1). Knockdown of SlRBP1 resembled the SlHYL1-RNAi semi-dwarf phenotype. Further studies revealed that the SlHYL1-SlRBP1 module additively promotes the expression of gibberellin (GA) biosynthetic genes, thereby facilitating GA accumulation. Additionally, the dwarf phenotypes of both SlHYL1-RNAi and SlRBP1-RNAi plants were partially rescued by exogenous GA(3) application. Notably, unlike SlHYL1, SlRBP1 did not affect the biogenesis of most miRNAs. In summary, our findings demonstrate that the SlHYL1-SlRBP1 module regulates tomato plant height by enhancing GA accumulation.
